thread:
Asha (Sec): Security advisory: new supply-chain requirement. All production artifacts (containers, wheels, wheels, npm packages, JVM jars, helm charts) must include an SBOM and be signed before publishing. Enforcement date: 2026-06-01. Read the summary and action items.
Jules (Build): Is this org-wide or just infra/product build pipelines?
Asha (Sec): Org-wide for anything that ends up in prod or customer-facing repos/artifact registries. Non-prod staging images encouraged to follow same rules. We're doing this to reduce unseen transitive vuln risk and enable quick attestation.
Nico (SupplyChain): Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/docs/security/sbom-signing. TL;DR: generate SBOM with syft/cyclonedx, upload SBOM to the artifact registry, sign artifact with cosign (or sign the SBOM), and attach provenance. CI templates will be updated.
Jules (Build): Quick examples for common build steps?
Omar (SecOps): Paste:
```
# container: build, sbom, sign
docker build -t registry.redwood/cool-service:1.2.3 .
syft registry.redwood/cool-service:1.2.3 -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json
cosign sign --key ~/.cosign/key.pub registry.redwood/cool-service:1.2.3
curl -X POST -F file=@sbom.json https://artifacts.redwood.internal/sboms/upload?artifact=registry.redwood/cool-service:1.2.3
```
```
# python wheel: build, sbom, sign
python -m build
syft dist/mypkg-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json
cosign sign-blob --key ~/.cosign/key.pub dist/mypkg-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl
```
Asha (Sec): CI enforcement: starting 2026-05-01 PRs that publish artifacts without SBOM+signature will fail the lint check. From 2026-06-01 the registry will reject unsigned artifacts. We will add clear failure messages so owners can fix quickly.
build-bot: New pipeline template published: infra/build-templates/sbom-signing.yml. It includes sbom generation, cosign step, and upload to the SBOM registry.
Nico (SupplyChain): For private keys: recommended pattern is to use KMS-backed ephemeral signing keys (cosign with KMS) or sigstore's ephemeral token flow. DO NOT store private keys in repo. If you need an offline key, register it with sec and escrow it.
Asha (Sec): Evidence of compliance: paste artifact URL + SBOM registry link + cosign verification output into ticket SEC-5120. We'll run automated audits and verify signatures.
Jules (Build): How do we handle third-party upstream images we base FROM? SBOM should include base layer data but what about signing?
Nico (SupplyChain): We require SBOM for our produced images that includes upstream packages. For upstream images that we don't control, CI must record the base image digest and include the upstream SBOM if available; otherwise note provenance and add a mitigation comment in SEC-5120 for review.
Omar (SecOps): Emergency workaround: if a critical rollout is blocked, infra lead can request a one-time waiver via SEC-5120 with justification; waivers expire in 48h and are audited.
sec-bot: Automated scanners scheduled: daily SBOM coverage report + signature verification sweep. Initial inventory shows ~67% of active prod artifacts already publish SBOM-like metadata; remaining owners listed in SEC-5120.
Asha (Sec): Action items: 1) owners update CI to produce SBOM and sign artifacts by 2026-05-01 for lint blocking. 2) complete signing+registry evidence by 2026-06-01 and paste in SEC-5120. 3) request exceptions explicitly in SEC-5120. 4) remove private signing keys from repos and adopt KMS/sigstore flows. We'll run office hours Tue 11am PT next two weeks to help teams.
Jules (Build): I'll open PRs to update our service templates and add a helper script that wraps syft+cosign and uploads to the SBOM registry.
Nico (SupplyChain): I'll publish a mapping of recommended tools per language and example CI snippets today.
Asha (Sec): Thanks. Ping me or sec-oncall for questions. Noncompliance after 2026-06-01 may result in publish blocks and required security review. :mag: :lock:
